newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: CDL Hotels sinks to new year low.
newsitem.headline: CDL Hotels sinks to new year low.

text.p: Shares in CDL Hotels International Ltd, the hotel arm of Singapore's City Developments Ltd, fell to a new year low on Monday on lingering disappointment over its 1996 results, dealers said.
At 0816 GMT, the stock was changing hands at HK$3.50, down 10 cents from its previous close. The stock touched a new year low of HK$3.475 earlier. Volume was 891,000 units.
Sandeep Mahawar, investment analyst with Deustche Morgan Grenfell, said the stock was down because of weak market sentiment and also there was still some disappointment over its 1996 results.
The group made net profit of HK$615 million, below market expectations of about HK$650 million.
Mahawar said the group's results were affected by weaker than expected hotel operations in Singapore and New Zealand.
On prospects, he said the profits should rise by about 10 percent this year to around HK$700 million.
"The main area of growth this year would be from Europe through Millennium & Copthorne," he said.
CDL owns 55 percent of Millennium & Copthorne Hotels, which holds the group's European and North American hotel interests.
